title: Repair F3/F4/F5: retry trace fidelity, v2 effect lifecycle admission, M12 deep equality
description:

---

## F3 — `retrieved_context` is false on an auditor-retry turn

**The defect.** `orchestrator.ts` computes `baseUserMessage` once, then on an
audit retry calls `runModelLoop` with `baseUserMessage + '\n\n' + correctiveNote`.
After acceptance the trace persists `retrievedContext: [baseUserMessage]`. So
the accepted narration and tool calls can describe attempt 2 while the
persisted input describes the pre-correction context. This PR's own comment on
`TurnTraceRecord.discoveryShadow`/`retrievedContext` now claims the field is
the message the model actually received, which makes the comment a false
statement rather than merely an omission.

**The repair.** Record the input the ACCEPTED attempt actually received.

Read `orchestrator.ts` around the attempt loop and `runModelLoop`'s call sites
first. Capture the exact user message used for the attempt that is accepted —
at the same place the accepted candidate's `narration` and `toolCalls` are
taken — and persist that. Do not reconstruct it afterwards by re-concatenating
`baseUserMessage` with the last corrective note: a reconstruction is a second
account of the input that can disagree with the one actually sent, which is
the defect in a new form. Record what was passed.

Every accepted attempt following one or more rejections is affected. Do not
special-case a single corrective note.

Keep `baseUserMessage` as the exact prefix property intact: the assembled
context is still a prefix of whatever the accepted attempt received, and the
packet still sits where injection put it.

**Evidence (`shadowRuntime.test.ts`, beside the existing intervene cases):**
- An `intervene` turn with a first-attempt audit REJECTION and second-attempt
  acceptance: capture the provider-neutral `ModelCompleteInput` the accepted
  attempt actually received (the scripted model already records `seen`), reread
  the trace out of SQLite, and assert `retrieved_context[0]` equals that exact
  string — including the corrective note.
- Assert in the same test that `delivery.renderedSha256` still equals the
  SHA-256 of the packet portion of that recorded message, so the binding
  survives the repair.
- A two-rejection case if the auditor's retry budget allows it; if it does not,
  say so explicitly in your notes rather than silently testing only one.
- The existing no-retry intervene case must still hold.

---

## F4 — the v2 reader admits impossible accepted-state-effect lifecycles

**The defect.** `RuntimeStateEffect` is by contract an effect of the ACCEPTED
candidate: a rejected attempt's writes roll back and contribute no event. The
reader already derives the real candidate-attempt count and constrains
capability invocations to attempts `1..attemptCount` (see `checkAudit`'s return
value and its use). `runtime.stateEffects` is constrained only to a
non-negative integer `attempt`, so it admits `0`, out-of-range attempts, and
effects attributed to a rejected attempt. `measureAcceptedStateEffect` then
pairs effects without consulting attempt identity, so malformed rejected-attempt
evidence can satisfy an accepted-turn expectation.

(The weak rule came from the parent bead's own spec. It is wrong; fix it.)

**The repair, in `shadow.ts`'s `assertV2`.** Apply the SAME lifecycle
constraint the capability events get, plus the constraints that follow from
`stateEffects` being one accepted attempt's stream:

- `attempt` is an integer in `1..attemptCount`, where `attemptCount` is the
  value the audit lifecycle already yields — reuse it, do not recompute it.
- All recorded effects share ONE attempt. They come from a single accepted
  candidate; two different attempt numbers in one array is an impossible
  producer output.
- `ordinal` values are the canonical positions of that one stream: integers
  starting at 0, strictly increasing, with no duplicates and no gaps.

Fail closed with `DiscoveryShadowSchemaError` in the established style. Keep the
validator's declared-here-not-imported discipline.

**Evidence (`shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts`, beside the existing
`accepted state effects` block):** reject each of — `attempt: 0`; an attempt
above the row's real candidate count; two effects with different attempts;
duplicate ordinals; a gap in ordinals; descending ordinals. Admit the
well-formed multi-effect stream. Each case must install an otherwise valid
effect stream first so no rejection passes vacuously.

---

## F5 — M12's argument comparison is not structural equality

**The defect.** `measureAcceptedStateEffect` compares declared argument values
with `JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b)`. Two structurally equal nested
objects whose keys were inserted in different orders therefore disagree. The
contract says each declared expected argument field DEEP-EQUALS the executed
value. P8's current expectation is flat strings and never exercises this.

**The repair, in `measurements.ts`.** Replace the stringify comparison with a
real structural deep equality: key-order-independent for objects, order- AND
length-significant for arrays, exact for primitives (including the
`null`/`undefined` distinction and `NaN` if you handle numbers generically).
Keep it small and local; do not add a dependency.

**Evidence (`stateEffectMeasurement.test.ts`):** nested objects with reordered
keys agree; arrays in a different order DISAGREE; a nested field with a
different value disagrees and names the top-level declared field; a declared
nested field absent from the executed args disagrees; extra executed keys
inside a declared nested object — decide deliberately whether the subset rule
recurses, state your decision in the doc comment and the bead notes, and test
the behaviour you chose.

---

- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the design

- House style: read the doc comments in `discovery/types.ts` and `shadow.ts`
  and match them. Every non-obvious shape says WHY it has that form and what

  shapes that could disagree.
- Known flake: `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs`
